claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives at home with you.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after him - I provide his food, clothes, and everything else he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A couple more questions:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation arranged by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he has been in care for a little while, but he still comes home to stay with me regularly - he spends quite a bit of time at home each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. I need to understand more about Alex's situation:

**How long has Alex been in care, and how much time does he spend at home with you each week? For example, does he stay overnight with you, and if so, how many nights per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in care for about 12 weeks now. He comes home to stay with me - it's more than a day a week, he spends quite a lot of time here. I'd say it's at least a full day and night each week, sometimes more.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify the specific amount of time Alex spends at home, as this is important for determining eligibility:

**Does Alex spend at least 2 nights in a row at home with you each week, or does he spend 7 or more days in a row at home with you at any time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he does spend at least 2 nights in a row at home with me each week - usually comes home for the weekends.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Here's why:

Even though Alex has been in care for 12 weeks (which is longer than the usual 8-week limit), there's an important exception that applies to your situation. According to the Child Benefit rules, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a child in care if they spend **at least 24 hours a week at home** with you.

Since Alex regularly comes home and spends at least 2 consecutive nights with you each week (usually on weekends), this clearly meets the 24-hour requirement. You also meet all the other eligibility criteria:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex and provide for his needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

### What you should do:

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you should apply. If you were previously receiving it but payments have stopped, you should contact HMRC to explain that Alex spends at least 2 nights in a row at home with you each week, which means you remain eligible.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
